global_boundaries: Do not add Linux, KVM, libvirt, LXC, ZFS, OVS, OVN, or purecvisorsd runtime code.
Do not add username-password login, token refresh, websocket event flow, or external CDN assets.
Do not render authorization token values or protected token file contents.
Do not run MSI, service, Hyper-V, firewall, trust-store, LAN, Event Log, update, rollback, or reboot mutation from frontend batches.
Keep public trusted signing and external stable publication as excluded or not-claimed unless separate evidence exists.

batches.title: Single UI shell contract and operator session controls
batches.objective: Lock the purecvisor-single visual/workbench contract into Desktop Node without importing non-Windows runtime routes.

work_items.title: Create the purecvisor-single to Desktop Node UI mapping table
acceptance: Mapping covers shell, menu, rail, asset explorer, tabbar, dashboard, status bar, and excludes Linux runtime surfaces.
verification: Pester static guard confirms design contract mentions Windows Desktop Node and does not import Single Edge runtime routes.

work_items.title: Reorder Web Console routes under the Single UI shell
acceptance: Dashboard, VM Workbench, Network, Jobs, Activity, Evidence, Troubleshooting, and Monitoring are reachable from the shell and preserve Desktop Node route names.
verification: Browser fixture activates each data-view-link without route mismatch.

work_items.title: Complete the left asset explorer for Windows VM assets
acceptance: VM asset rows support search, status, selected state, and empty state; container tab remains disabled or absent.
verification: Static guard matches vm-asset-list, vm-filter, asset-status, and no container runtime route strings.

work_items.title: Wire the top menu bar commands
acceptance: Refresh, open dashboard, open VM workbench, open network, open evidence, open troubleshooting, and clear browser state commands call existing frontend handlers.
verification: Browser fixture clicks menu command markers and observes active view or refresh state.

work_items.title: Bind operator session, organization, language, and Live viewer UI
acceptance: Session label, organization selector, Korean language indicator, Live viewer state, token state, and logout boundary render as Desktop Node local console state.
verification: Pester guard confirms shell controls exist and no password-login or token-refresh route is introduced.

batches.title: Dashboard, VM detail, lifecycle, and checkpoint workbench
batches.objective: Finish the VM operator loop from summary to lifecycle jobs while keeping mutations behind installed Local API calls only.

work_items.title: Bind dashboard summary cards to real API state
acceptance: Host readiness, service status, VM count, active jobs, recent warnings, and batch evidence status derive from loaded API payloads or explicit degraded state.
verification: Browser fixture covers available, degraded, and API failure dashboard states.

work_items.title: Finish VM list filtering, sorting, search, and selection
acceptance: VM list supports text filter, state filter, stable sort, selected row sync with asset explorer, and clear empty result copy.
verification: Browser fixture filters VM rows and verifies selected VM detail remains coherent.

work_items.title: Expand VM detail for status, CPU, memory, storage, network, and checkpoints
acceptance: VM detail panel renders state, generation, CPU, memory, storage, network switch, console availability, managed marker, and checkpoint count.
verification: Static and browser fixture checks cover populated, missing, and native structured failure states.

work_items.title: Complete VM lifecycle action UX
acceptance: Create, start, shutdown, poweroff, restart, and delete actions show confirmation where destructive, scoped pending state, job tracking, disabled state, and structured failure recovery.
verification: Browser fixture validates pending buttons, PCV_VM_DELETE_RUNNING_BLOCKED, PCV_VM_NOT_MANAGED_BY_PURECVISOR, and tracked job insertion.

work_items.title: Complete checkpoint create, restore, and delete UX
acceptance: Checkpoint actions use existing API registry, scoped checkpoint pending state, confirmation for restore/delete, job tracking, and clear failure rows.
verification: Browser fixture covers checkpoint list loaded, create queued, restore queued, delete queued, and failure problem details rendering.

batches.title: Activity, network inventory, diagnostic bundle, and token handoff
batches.objective: Finish operational read and recovery surfaces without browser-side host mutation.

work_items.title: Finish job queue and activity pagination
acceptance: Jobs support first page, next page, retention summary, retry, cancel, stale polling guard, and no duplicate tracked rows.
verification: Browser fixture covers next_offset, cancel, retry, and stale refresh suppression.

work_items.title: Unify pending action, optimistic state, disabled state, and recovery
acceptance: All VM, checkpoint, job, refresh, and diagnostic actions use stable pending keys and recover on success, failure, abort, and stale response.
verification: Browser fixture asserts no button remains disabled after rejected API calls.

work_items.title: Rebuild network inventory in Single UI style
acceptance: Network inventory displays switch type, default flag, management OS flag, external adapter description, source, and read-only boundary.
verification: Pester guard confirms network inventory route and no switch, IP, firewall, or network mutation command strings.

work_items.title: Complete diagnostic bundle create and download UI
acceptance: Diagnostic bundle panel calls POST create and authenticated GET download through API client, shows bundle id, redaction boundary, retention status, and error contract.
verification: Browser fixture covers create 201, download 200, authorization-required failure, and redacted token boundary.

work_items.title: Finish token rotation and browser token clear UX
acceptance: Panel distinguishes browser token clear from service protected-token mutation, renders storage path boundary, and updates connection state after clear.
verification: Pester guard confirms no service token mutation command text and no authorization credential literal.

batches.title: Error contracts, service health, evidence dashboard, fixtures, and service-layer tests
batches.objective: Make frontend service logic robust against backend problem details, partial failures, and evidence degradation.

work_items.title: Integrate timeout, rate-limit, and problem-details error display
acceptance: PCV_RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, PCV_ROUTE_TIMEOUT, Retry-After, request_id, route_timeout_seconds, and nested details render as readable operator rows.
verification: Browser fixture covers 429 and 504 problem-details JSON without displaying [object Object].

work_items.title: Finish service health, listener, and runtime policy status panels
acceptance: Panels show service running, Local API listener scope, runtime policy, token policy, LAN exposure, timeout, rate limit, and request burst settings.
verification: Browser fixture covers runtime policy available, missing, and degraded states.

work_items.title: Complete batch evidence dashboard
acceptance: Evidence view displays latest batch id, route/MSI/Hyper-V status, OS mutation status, GPU snapshots, artifact paths, pass/fail/degraded/missing states, and public-boundary labels.
verification: Browser fixture covers available, missing, unavailable, degraded, malformed, and sanitized evidence states.

work_items.title: Normalize mock fixture and installed listener API switch behavior
acceptance: Fixture mode and installed listener mode share route registry, token handling, error normalization, and no direct mutation command strings.
verification: npm run verify:parity --prefix web passes and fixture route coverage matches DESKTOP_NODE_API_ROUTES.

work_items.title: Add frontend service layer tests for API client, refresh lifecycle, and error mapping
acceptance: Tests cover route registry, abort/stale refresh, partial refresh degradation, error detail formatting, rate-limit, timeout, and redaction boundary.
verification: Invoke-Pester and npm test both fail before missing behavior and pass after implementation.

batches.title: Browser parity, visual polish, responsive/a11y pass, and final evidence
batches.objective: Close the frontend completion loop with browser fixture coverage, CSS polish, responsive behavior, accessibility, and evidence publication.

work_items.title: Broaden browser fixture and parity tests
acceptance: Browser fixture covers all active views, shell commands, VM action pending states, network, evidence, diagnostics, token, rate-limit, and timeout states.
verification: npm run verify:parity --prefix web passes with expanded fixture assertions.

work_items.title: Complete CSS and visual polish
acceptance: Spacing, typography, dark surfaces, teal accent, scrollbars, focus, hover, disabled, loading, destructive, warning, success, and table states match the Single UI clone contract.
verification: Pester static guard confirms tokens, component classes, and no one-hue or decorative hero imports.

work_items.title: Finish responsive layout for ultrawide, desktop, tablet, and narrow viewports
acceptance: No incoherent overlap at 344px, 480px, 768px, 1024px, 1440px, and ultrawide; tables scroll or collapse predictably; button text fits.
verification: Browser fixture viewport checks and static CSS guard confirm responsive breakpoints.

work_items.title: Complete accessibility pass
acceptance: Interactive controls have labels or aria-labels, focus ring remains visible, active view uses aria-current, dialogs preserve keyboard affordances, and status updates expose text equivalents.
verification: Pester guard scans required aria labels and browser fixture checks keyboard navigation for primary view links/actions.

work_items.title: Publish final static asset, parity, smoke, and evidence closure
acceptance: Final docs list implementation scope, excluded host mutation, verification commands, screenshot or fixture paths, and public-boundary non-claims.
verification: All final_verification_commands pass and evidence document states frontend-only, no host mutation, no public trusted signing, no external stable publication.
